I5.quote: The adsorption of permanent gases on graphite, graphene, nanotubes, layers of fullerenes, and other graphitic materials has attracted considerable interest.
I5.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 074311-1), Section I. Introduction

notes: Experimental part: 'Helium droplets are doped with fullerenes (either C60 or C70) and hydrogen (H2 or D2) and investigated by high-resolution mass spectrometry.' (main, p. 2, Abstract). Hydrogen is picked up at a partial pressure of 'typically a few times 10-3 Pa' by droplets at about 0.37 K (main, p. 3, Section II); the reported quantity is ion abundance (arb. units) versus cluster size n (main, p. 6, Fig. 4), not an amount of H2 taken up per mass of sorbent. Theory part: DFT energies for C60Hx, x = 1-5 (Tables I-II). The paper is experimental, not purely theoretical, and not electrochemical, so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated. No surface area is reported anywhere. Not a review, not retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction notice in the PDF). PDF page 1 is a publisher cover sheet, so PDF page numbers are one higher than journal page numbers.
